No whole-paper, whole-guidance, private screenshot, mobile/browser, accessibility, independent, expert, owner, learner or native-language acceptance. The two support bodies have no teaching points or approval credit.

points.requirement: The same recognition module can have a different physical and functional job after reformatting.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A recognition domain can behave differently when built into a different therapeutic structure. Its final format is part of the experiment.
evidence.explanation: The selected fields carry the specified format distinction at the stated model or inference scope. A dedicated format definition is carried only by the actual unmerged owner. The source diagram is illustrative, not a clinical format comparison. This is an actual unmerged contributor field, not root integration.

points.requirement: A soluble assembly has no intracellular receptor tail; a membrane CAR is a receptor on a living cell.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A dosed T-cell engager supplies a protein connecting target recognition to an available T cell. It does not itself install receptor instructions or supply engineered living responders.
evidence.explanation: The selected fields carry the specified format distinction at the stated model or inference scope. The P20 object distinction is reused at its exact current field and reader hashes. The soluble example does not supply engineered cells or its own intracellular signalling chain. This is a current registered local-root field, not main or live acceptance.

points.requirement: The CAR example connects external recognition through a spacer and membrane-spanning segment to intracellular signalling.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A common CAR presents a binder outside the cell and signaling domains inside it, connected through a spacer and transmembrane region.
evidence.explanation: The selected fields carry the specified format distinction at the stated model or inference scope. Current CAR anatomy and the previously read FDA construct section supply external recognition, spacer, membrane and internal signalling. The illustrated receptor crosses the effector-cell membrane, not both cells. This is a current registered local-root field, not main or live acceptance.

points.requirement: Contact between opposed cell surfaces constrains reach and geometry; the receptor does not itself traverse both cells.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Suppose two fictional CARs differ only in their hinge: both bind purified antigen, but only one kills antigen-bearing cells. Compare surface expression and the geometry of cell contact before concluding that affinity is the problem.
evidence.explanation: The selected fields carry the specified format distinction at the stated model or inference scope. Current fields connect cell-contact geometry, surface expression and membrane anchoring. The two opposing surfaces are a checked schematic context, not a universal quantitative gap or a second transmembrane crossing. This is a current registered local-root field, not main or live acceptance.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A common antibody-derived CAR joins an external binding region, a hinge or spacer, a membrane anchor and intracellular signaling domains.
evidence.explanation: The selected fields carry the specified format distinction at the stated model or inference scope. Current fields connect cell-contact geometry, surface expression and membrane anchoring. The two opposing surfaces are a checked schematic context, not a universal quantitative gap or a second transmembrane crossing. This is a current registered local-root field, not main or live acceptance.

points.requirement: A soluble assembled protein needs appropriate folding, stability, distribution and useful action under its intended conditions.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Format changes what is tested. A soluble molecule must stay intact and usable through manufacture, storage and exposure, and adding binding units or a chemical cargo can change its behaviour (Junutula et al., 2008, anti-MUC16 conjugate in mice, rats and monkeys). A CAR fixes the binder to a membrane and links contact to signalling, so spacer reach, target position, expression and clustering matter (Hudecek et al., 2015; Long et al., 2015). The same recognition sequence therefore does not guarantee the same performance.
evidence.explanation: The current owner carries general stability, intactness, usability and exposure; the named drawn folding/distribution clauses are not credited until the proposed text is applied. Junutula abstract describes cysteine-engineered conjugates without perturbing immunoglobulin folding/assembly and compares animal-model properties. The current owner explicitly carries stability and exposure, but not the complete folding/distribution phrasing drawn in the figure. The proposed completion is labelled as a schematic reading rule, not a new measured result. This is an actual unmerged contributor field, not root integration.

remaining: Explicit folding and distribution wording for the illustrated soluble format is not present in the selected current format-owner text. Exact proposed completion remains unapplied.

points.requirement: Spacer context, receptor expression and clustering are separate requirements of the assembled CAR format.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A CAR fixes the binder to a membrane and links contact to signalling, so spacer reach, target position, expression and clustering matter (Hudecek et al., 2015; Long et al., 2015). The same recognition sequence therefore does not guarantee the same performance.
evidence.explanation: The selected fields carry the specified format distinction at the stated model or inference scope. Hudecek abstract concerns length/composition of specified IgG-derived spacers and Fc interactions. Long abstract concerns antigen-independent scFv clustering in the studied CARs. These examples do not make every spacer, expression problem or binder behave identically. This is an actual unmerged contributor field, not root integration.

points.requirement: Clustering can cause antigen-independent signalling in particular CAR constructs; this is not a claim that all binders cluster.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Antigen-independent clustering of scFvs triggered tonic CD3-zeta signalling and early exhaustion in the CARs studied, except the CD19 CAR, with 4-1BB reducing and CD28 increasing the effect (Long et al., 2015).
evidence.explanation: The selected fields carry the specified format distinction at the stated model or inference scope. Long abstract identifies tonic CD3-zeta phosphorylation and early exhaustion from antigen-independent scFv clustering in studied constructs, with the CD19 exception and CD28/4-1BB comparison retained. No clinical ranking across all products is inferred. This is an actual unmerged contributor field, not root integration.

points.requirement: Isolated affinity or one architecture does not establish universally better activity, safety or efficacy.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: The manufacturing evaluation includes molecular identity, correct pairing, aggregation, fragments, stability and biological potency. Affinity, binding kinetics, avidity, target distribution and exposure belong to the actual format. Two successful binding assays do not by themselves demonstrate the intended combined function.
evidence.explanation: The selected fields carry the specified format distinction at the stated model or inference scope. Junutula, Hudecek and Long are construct-specific studies. FDA printed pages21 to22 explicitly warn that products sharing a recognition domain can have different safety profiles. The no-ranking conclusion is an evidence boundary, not proof of an optimal architecture. This is a current registered local-root field, not main or live acceptance.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Generation labels describe common signaling architectures. First-generation constructs use an activation domain, often CD3 zeta; second-generation designs add one costimulatory region; third-generation designs combine two. Fourth-generation and later labels vary across authors. More domains do not establish better patient outcomes. The full binder, spacer, anchor, signaling arrangement and cell preparation still matter.
evidence.explanation: The selected fields carry the specified format distinction at the stated model or inference scope. Junutula, Hudecek and Long are construct-specific studies. FDA printed pages21 to22 explicitly warn that products sharing a recognition domain can have different safety profiles. The no-ranking conclusion is an evidence boundary, not proof of an optimal architecture. This is a current registered local-root field, not main or live acceptance.

points.requirement: The complete intended format needs testing; an isolated binder result is not proven portable performance.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A change of format is a new product hypothesis. If an ADC binds M but yields little active material after uptake, an M-directed engager might avoid that particular processing requirement. It still needs its own binding and contact-geometry measurements, useful effector access and function, normal-tissue testing and clinical evidence. Earlier antibody or ADC tolerability does not establish the safety of a different action. Bystander delivery and two-address designs are possible responses to heterogeneous expression, not guaranteed coverage or an exhaustive list of solutions.
evidence.explanation: The selected fields carry the specified format distinction at the stated model or inference scope. FDA nonclinical guidance concerns ex vivo-manufactured CAR T products. Its product differences and the three named experimental examples support testing a complete intended format. No general clinical outcome or universal assay cutoff is introduced. This is a current registered local-root field, not main or live acceptance.
